claims.text: Atom Probe Tomography can elucidate mechanistic aspects and elemental redistribution of nanoprecipitates during oxidation of Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 HEA.
APT provides near-atomic-resolution three-dimensional compositional maps.
APT can reveal interfacial compositional gradients and segregation produced during high-temperature exposure.
The additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 HEA contains dual nanoprecipitation phases.
The additively manufactured alloy has enhanced strength relative to cast and wrought counterparts.
The nanoprecipitates may undergo elemental segregation and interfacial modification during oxidation.
Differential diffusion rates among the alloy constituents cause elemental segregation at matrix–nanoprecipitate interfaces during high-temperature oxidation.
Differences in oxygen affinity among the alloy constituents cause elemental segregation at matrix–nanoprecipitate interfaces.
Redistribution of Al and Ti can contribute to protective oxide formation or compromise oxidation resistance.
APT will capture subtle nanoscale compositional gradients associated with oxidation.
Oxidized specimens will exhibit elemental enrichment or depletion around nanoprecipitates relative to the bulk matrix.
The nanoprecipitate-associated elemental gradients will correlate with improvements or degradations in oxidation resistance.
Non-oxidized samples have uniform elemental distributions across the nanoprecipitates and matrix.
The proposed APT approach is applicable to HEAs with dual nanoprecipitation phases under high-temperature oxidation conditions.
Results may not transfer directly to alloys with different precipitate chemistries or microstructures.
Experimental challenges in capturing in-situ high-temperature dynamics may limit quantitative gradients and their correlation with oxidation kinetics.
